blockingIssues.title: I5: `arrived` reservations are movable by planBooking/tryRepair and reflow
blockingIssues.description: packages/reservations/src/engine/day-state.ts:118-133 `isBookingHardLocked` locks only seated/partially_seated, tableLocked and the freeze window; `arrived` is in ACTIVE_BOOKING_STATUSES (assign.ts:269-275) and therefore soft, so repair and reflow move it. VAL-FND-007 requires that neither tryRepair nor reflow ever moves a reservation in partially_arrived/arrived/partially_seated/seated/finished. (`partially_arrived` does not exist in the 13-status model; `arrived` does.) The worker's I5 test omits the arrived case.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Treat arrived (and any seated-adjacent status present in the model) as hard-locked in isBookingHardLocked and add the arrived case to the I5 test.

blockingIssues.title: Engine expansion budgets attached to the wrong operations (book 200 vs 2,000; reflow 2,000 vs 5,000)
blockingIssues.description: assign.ts:23-24 defines MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS=200 and MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS=2_000; planBooking caps at min(200, input.maxExpansions) (assign.ts:458-461) so a caller cannot raise the book budget, and reflowDay caps at min(2_000, ...) (assign.ts:918-921). VAL-FND-009, mission.md §9 and architecture.md:1196-1197 require search 200 per slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000, with 'no fit' rather than a partial plan when exhausted. A 201-2,000-expansion book returns a false repair_budget_exhausted. The scale test and features.json wording enshrine the wrong mapping.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Introduce per-operation budgets (search 200/slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000), relax the min() caps accordingly, and update the scale test expectations.

blockingIssues.title: validateConfig misses required detections and returns a report object instead of ConfigIssue[]
blockingIssues.description: validate.ts: no check that turn-time buckets cover 1..party_max contiguously (only gaps/overlaps between existing buckets, gaps as warnings), no `end_min - first_seating_min <= 1440` span check (no 1440 anywhere in the file), no policies input so invalid policy references are never detected, no strict Zod blocks schema in src/config/, and the return type is ValidateConfigReport (validate.ts:121-140), not ConfigIssue[]. VAL-FND-004 requires all of these.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add first-bucket-starts-at-1 and last-bucket-reaches-party_max coverage errors, the 1440 span check, a policies field with reference validation, a blocks schema, and either return ConfigIssue[] or add a contract-conformant wrapper.

blockingIssues.title: localToInstant lacks the contract's opts parameter and gap:'skip'/'after' and overlap semantics
blockingIssues.description: time.ts:68-114 is localToInstant(businessDate, localStartMin, timeZone) returning {instantMs, adjustedForGap, ambiguousFold}, never null; gap minutes always resolve to the post-gap instant and folds always pick the earlier occurrence. VAL-FND-003 requires opts (`{gap:'skip'|'after', overlap:'earlier'|'later'}`), null + gap:'skip' for booking slots, gap:'after' for service ends, and overlap:'later' where ends resolve. resolveServiceWindow (time.ts:174-194) resolves ends through the same path. time.test.ts uses 2026-03-08/2026-03-29 instead of the contract's 2027-03-14/2027-03-28 and never exercises the 90-minute fold or the day_start_min ±1 boundary.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add the opts parameter and result union (null for skipped gaps), use gap:'after'/overlap:'later' for service windows, and add the contract's dated cases.

blockingIssues.title: Staff channels hide pacing-breached slots; walk_in_only not allowed for waitlist; channel model incomplete
blockingIssues.description: availability.ts:516-518 `if (!globalPacing.allowed) continue` drops the slot for every channel; SearchAvailabilityResult has no warnings field; pacing.ts returns allowed:false for slot covers/parties regardless of channel. isModeAllowedForChannel (day-state.ts:97-110) allows walk_in_only only for walk_in, and BookingChannel (day-state.ts:3-4) lacks native/voice_agent/host/waitlist. VAL-FND-006 requires staff channels to surface pacing breaches as warnings and allow walk_in_only tables for walk_in and waitlist.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Return pacing breaches as warnings for staff channels instead of dropping slots, extend the channel set, and allow walk_in_only for waitlist.

blockingIssues.title: No deadline response schemas with ISO expiresAt + server now
blockingIssues.description: grep for expiresAt/now across packages/reservations/src/schemas returns no matches; the schemas are request DTOs plus internal context/tick payloads. VAL-FND-008 requires strict DTOs where every deadline response (hold, payment, large-party request, waitlist offer, notify-me) includes ISO `expiresAt` and server `now`.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add deadline response schemas with expiresAt/now and tests.

blockingIssues.title: Property suite does not run random operation sequences and does not verify I1-I8
blockingIssues.description: engine.property.test.ts runs 300 static day scenarios (one assignTables + one search each); no random operation sequences (search/hold/book/modify/cancel/seat/finish/no-show/block/settings/clock) and no per-step invariant verification. testing/oracle.ts verifyDayInvariants checks only I1-I4 equivalents (double booking incl. holds, party-size bounds, active membership, blocks) and never I5-I8; the test title claims I1-I7 while VAL-FND-009 requires I1 through I8 and zero soundness failures.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add an operation-sequence property test that applies each op and re-verifies the full invariant set (including I5-I8) against the oracle after every step.

blockingIssues.title: Weekly service templates not ordered by latest effective_from then priority
blockingIssues.description: rules/resolve-services.ts sortServices (lines 226-230) sorts by sortOrder -> startMin -> id; there is no `priority` field in WeeklyServiceTemplateInput and effective_from/to are only date-range filters. VAL-FND-005 requires ordering by latest effective_from, then priority (architecture.md:618).
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add the priority input field and sort by effective_from desc then priority before sortOrder.

blockingIssues.title: Occupancy overlap triggers omit the required `o.overbook = 0` predicate
blockingIssues.description: packages/tenant-db/drizzle/0016_reservations_foundation.sql:807-813 and 820-827 match another row with only `o.active = 1`; VAL-FND-011 and architecture.md §4.8 require `active = 1 AND overbook = 0`, because explicit staff overbook rows must not block a normal occupancy. Reproduced read-only: after an overbook row [1000,2000), a normal INSERT [1500,2500) aborts with 'table_overlap'. The domain engine deliberately ignores overbook rows (packages/reservations/src/engine/occupancy.ts:94,117,166; testing/oracle.ts:114), so engine-validated writes can fail at the DB.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add `AND o.overbook = 0` to both EXISTS predicates and add a test where a normal occupancy overlaps an existing overbook row and must succeed.

blockingIssues.title: Trigger abort message is 'table_overlap', not the contract's 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap'
blockingIssues.description: SQL:806/819 raise 'table_overlap'; VAL-FND-011 and architecture §4.8 require 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap'. The test asserts the wrong string (reservations-schema.test.ts:1177/1210/1251), and the only consumer, apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-write.ts:571-581 mapSqliteConstraintError, matches 'overlap_conflict' (no artifact raises that), so trigger aborts are not mapped to 409. Docs/ADR 048 use 'table_overlap' too.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Pick the contract string, change both RAISE calls + test expectations + mapSqliteConstraintError together (and align the docs).

blockingIssues.title: Tenant-db schema test reads a gitignored, untracked artifact with no generator in its task graph
blockingIssues.description: packages/tenant-db/src/reservations-schema.test.ts:131-144 does an unguarded readFileSync of apps/tenant-api/workers/migrations.generated.ts. `git check-ignore -v` confirms apps/tenant-api/.gitignore:1 ignores it, `git ls-files` shows it untracked, turbo's test task depends only on ^build (tenant-api is not a tenant-db dependency), and CI's vitest job (.github/workflows/deploy.yml:173-223) runs no build, so `npm test -w @repo/tenant-db` fails with ENOENT on a clean checkout/CI. It passes here only because a worker generated the file.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Generate the DO bundle inside the test setup (or an existsSync-guarded skip), or move the sync assertion to a tenant-api-owned test whose task dependency generates it.

blockingIssues.title: Reservations context cache uses 60 s/5 min with no failure cooldown
blockingIssues.description: apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-context.ts:10-11,18-21,76-99: 60 s fresh, 5 min stale LRU, no failure cooldown (every request past 60 s re-fetches even after failures). VAL-FND-018 and architecture.md:456-459 require 5 min fresh, 24 h stale, 30 s failure cooldown, 3 s timeout, redirect:'error' (copy lib/scope-context.ts). The shipped test asserts the deviating values.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Adopt the scope-context parameters (5 min/24 h/30 s cooldown) and update the test.

blockingIssues.title: No `hasProvisionedDb` check on reservations paths
blockingIssues.description: The shared check ensureActiveOrgInNodeRegion (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-operator.ts:30-47) verifies active + region only; rsvGuard/reservations-auth.ts never look up the organization; grep finds hasProvisionedDb in reservations files only in the security-test fixture. VAL-FND-017 requires an active and provisioned organization, and staff-auth.ts:167 is the mirror that returns 404. An active-but-unprovisioned org is served a freshly created empty tenant DB instead of a uniform refusal.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Return 404 from ensureActiveOrgInNodeRegion when organization.hasProvisionedDb is false and add a sweep case.

blockingIssues.title: Security sweep omits tenant-api-operator audience, over-long TTL and impersonated-write variants
blockingIssues.description: apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-security.test.ts: mintRsvToken exposes ttlSeconds (line 118) and impersonated (line 117) but no case uses them; the only wrong audience tested is 'tenant-api-staffing' (line 225). VAL-FND-020 requires every operator route to be swept for wrong-audience including staffing and tenant-api-operator tokens, over-long TTL (401) and impersonated-write (403); cross-org/cross-location are spot-checked on two routes rather than every route. library/staffing-patterns.md:94 lists the same variants.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Add the three token variants (and cross-org/cross-location) to the existing per-route loops.

blockingIssues.title: Location picker never hidden for a single-location organization
blockingIssues.description: apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/reservations+/_layout.tsx:182-209 always renders the Location select and only special-cases locations.length === 0; no length === 1 branch exists. VAL-FND-022 requires hiding the location picker when the organization has only one location (riyadh-grill renders a one-option selector).
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Render the picker only when locations.length > 1 (staffing's pattern).

blockingIssues.title: Docs list a permission/claim/audience vocabulary that does not exist in code
blockingIssues.description: docs/permissions.md:186-242 lists read/update:reservations:any, read/update:guestbook:any, read:reservations_settings:any, read:reservations_reports:any, refund:reservations_payments:any, migration 0023 and `imp: true`; docs/reservations-contract.md and ADR 048 repeat aud 'tenant-api-reservations', claims org/reg/scp/imp, header X-Internal-Token. The implemented strings are the contract's: 8 read|update:reservation* permissions, aud 'tenant-api-reservations-operator', claims orgId/region/scope/impersonated, Bearer INTERNAL_COMMAND_TOKEN, migration 0025, and the 6 reservations.* flags are not listed. VAL-FND-024 requires docs/permissions.md to list the 8 permissions and 6 flags.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Rewrite the reservations sections of docs/permissions.md, docs/reservations-contract.md and ADR 048 to the implemented vocabulary (code + contract as source of truth).

nonBlockingObservations.description: messages.ts defaults quiet hours to 22:00-08:00 and shifts sends later (next 08:00); architecture.md:1634 and VAL-MSG-016 say 21:00-08:00 with sends moved earlier (or skipped). Not a foundation blocker, but the guest-messages milestone will fail until corrected.

MESSAGE_KINDS names diverge from architecture §9.3 (modified vs modification, cancelled vs cancellation_guest/restaurant, reminder_24h/2h vs reminder, waitlist_table_ready vs waitlist_ready, notify_slot_opened vs notify_available); later milestones assert these names in meta.messageKind and email captures.

state-machine.ts has pending_approval/disputed and no partially_arrived; VAL-ONLINE later uses status `requested`; consumesCapacity excludes pending_payment although architecture §6.4 says a pending_payment booking consumes capacity until payment_expires_at.

tenant-api customer auth now rejects phone numbers without a leading '+' that the previous helper accepted (packages/reservations/src/phone.ts requires E.164 with '+'); undocumented behavior change in a shared auth path. Decide whether E.164-only is intended and document it.

rsv_holds_single_conversion uses WHEN OLD.status='converted' AND NEW.status='converted' instead of the contract's any-update-on-a-converted-hold; latent because hold_id UNIQUE still guarantees at-most-once conversion. One-line tightening recommended with the trigger fix.

role-presets.ts defines 7 presets (host, shift_manager, reservations_manager, guest_relations, guestbook_manager, finance, owner); the contract's 4 named presets carry the exact required grants, so this is additive. VAL-FND-015 wording ('the 4 presets') could be relaxed to the 4 required sets.

ADR 048 omits guest identity without login, the payments split, the shared org alarm and messaging regions; VAL-FND-024's bar is existence + headings, so non-blocking, but the topics should be added while the feature is in context.

reservations-write.ts: on an idempotency replay the transaction returns after the expiry sweep and skips the day-version bump for dates freed by that sweep. Narrow consistency gap; no capacity correctness break.

POST /setup/locations/:locationId/settings (reservations-operator.ts:133-186) writes rsv_location_settings outside withReservationWrite and does not bump rsv_day_versions; the setup milestone should route it through the gate.

reservations-public.ts:68-74 fails open when the App context is null (config/holds answer without a flag check); architecture requires fail-closed 503 for public writes. Scaffold-only today; online-booking must not inherit it.
notifyReservationsContextChanged has no caller, so no App mutation evicts the regional context cache; wire it into the actions the later milestones own.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Reconcile the engine budget wording: the fnd-zoned-time-and-reservations-domain expectedBehavior says MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS=200 / MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS=2000, while validation-contract.md VAL-FND-009, mission.md §9 and architecture.md:1196-1197 require search 200 per slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000. The worker implemented features.json's numbers; make the record defer to the contract so later workers are not misled.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: features.json expectedBehavior bullet 5 vs validation-contract.md VAL-FND-009; packages/reservations/src/engine/assign.ts:23-24,458-461,918-921

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Enumerate the security-gate requirements in the skill/AGENTS 'Security gates' bullet: the reservations sweep must include the tenant-api-operator audience (not only staffing), an over-long TTL token, an impersonated-write token, cross-org and cross-location variants on every mounted route, and the guard must refuse an active-but-unprovisioned org (404) like staff-auth.ts:167. Both gaps shipped despite being in library/staffing-patterns.md:43,94.

State that VAL-FND-009 needs a random operation-sequence property test verifying invariants I1-I8 after every step (the library already lists them at engine-notes.md:201-210), and that deviations from architecture API names must be recorded in the handoff (this worker reported followedProcedure=true with an empty deviations list while shipping localToInstant without opts, a report-object validateConfig and different channel/status vocabularies).

Fix contract text traps a validator will trip over: VAL-FND-010 says 'all 30 rsv_* tables' but enumerates 41 (implementation has 41); VAL-FND-013's evidence SQL filters `WHERE A LIKE 'org_perm_%'` although A is the role id and B the permission id in _OrganizationPermissionToRole (use `WHERE B LIKE '%reservation%'`); decide one canonical overlap abort string (contract/architecture say 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap', ADR 048/reservations-plan say 'table_overlap'); VAL-FND-007 names `partially_arrived`, which is not in the 13-status model; VAL-FND-015 says 'the 4 presets' where the code has 7 (the four required sets are exact).

Add one canonical-vocabulary line for the reservations module (8 permission strings, 6 flag keys, token claim names, Bearer INTERNAL_COMMAND_TOKEN) and state that code + validation contract govern until the repo docs are reconciled; docs/permissions.md, docs/reservations-contract.md and ADR 048 currently describe a different vocabulary.
